h1: How Should a Strapless Bra Fit?
keywords: how should a strapless bra fit
how is a strapless bra supposed to fit
how are strapless bras supposed to fit
answer: A strapless bra fits when the band is noticeably firmer than your everyday bra, sits level and doesn't slip when you raise your arms, the silicone grip holds without pinching, the cups enclose your breasts with no gaping at the top, and the wires sit on your ribs, not on breast tissue.
intro: With no straps, the band does every bit of the work, so it has to be firm. Many people wear a strapless bra one band size smaller than their regular bra, with the cup letter up one to keep the same volume. Test it standing, sitting, raising your arms and twisting side to side; if it creeps down at any point, it won't last an evening.

checklist.good: Firm, level and anchored on the loosest or middle hook. You can slide one finger under it, and it stays in place when you lift both arms over your head.
checklist.tooTight: It digs in hard, makes the sides bulge noticeably, or makes it hard to breathe or sit comfortably.
checklist.tooLoose: It slides down, rotates, or needs hitching up after a few minutes. Go down a band size.

checklist.good: The cups enclose your breasts with the top edge lying flat. Strapless cups are often cut a little lower and wider to hold from below and the sides.
checklist.tooTight: Tissue spills over the top or at the sides, or the edges cut into the breast.
checklist.tooLoose: The top of the cup gapes or folds over, especially when you bend forward.

checklist.good: The wires sit in the fold under your breasts and wrap back along your ribs. Strapless wires are often longer at the sides for extra hold.
checklist.tooTight: The wires press on breast tissue at the sides or under the arms.
checklist.tooLoose: The wires lift away from your ribs or slide down below the breast fold.

checklist.good: Lies flat against your breastbone, anchoring the front so the cups can't tip forward.
checklist.tooTight: Presses or rubs painfully on the breastbone.
checklist.tooLoose: Floats away from your chest, which lets the bra pull downward over time.

checklist.good: The upper edge and any silicone strip sit flat against your skin and grip without leaving deep marks.
checklist.tooTight: Silicone pinches, rubs or leaves raw marks after a short wear.
checklist.tooLoose: The edge lifts off your skin, letting the cups peel away and the bra slide.

variations.heading: Types of strapless bra
variations.intro: Choose the style by bust size and outfit, then fit the band firmly.

items.name: Standard strapless underwire
items.text: A wide, firm band with silicone grip at the top and bottom edges. Most people can wear one for an evening if the band fits snugly. Wider side wings give more hold on fuller busts.

items.name: Longline or bustier
items.text: The band extends down toward the waist, spreading the grip over more of the torso. Often the most secure option for D cups and above, and for long events. The bottom edge should lie flat without rolling.

items.name: Convertible (multiway)
items.text: Wears strapless or with straps in halter, crossover or one-shoulder positions. Fit the band as for a strapless bra, then use the straps only as a backup.

items.name: Bandeau
items.text: A tube of stretch fabric with light or no padding. It suits smaller busts and casual wear; it offers little lift and depends entirely on the band being snug.

items.name: Adhesive and backless
items.text: Cups that stick to the skin, for open-back dresses. They work best for smaller busts. Skin must be clean and dry, without lotion, for them to hold.

measure.heading: How to size a strapless bra
measure.intro: Start from your measured band-and-cup size, then go firmer on the band.
steps: Measure snugly around your ribcage directly under your breasts after exhaling, keeping the tape level. Round to the nearest even number for your band size.
Measure loosely around the fullest part of your bust and subtract the band size. Each inch is one cup: 1 in A, 2 in B, 3 in C, 4 in D, 5 in DD.
Try your measured size. If it slips, try the sister size one band smaller and one cup larger (for example 34C to 32D).
Raise your arms, sit, and twist. A good strapless bra stays put through all three.
Check it under the actual dress or top, since necklines, boning and fabric weight change how it feels.
measure.tip: Buy a strapless bra a few weeks before an event, so you have time to swap sizes and wear it around the house to make sure it's comfortable for hours.

sizeTable.caption: Strapless bra band size conversions
sizeTable.note: EU bands are underbust centimeters rounded to the nearest 5; French bands add 15. When you go down a band for a strapless bra, go up a cup letter to keep the same cup volume.

problems.problem: The bra slides down during the day
problems.fix: The band is too loose. Go down a band size and up a cup (sister size), or switch to a longline style with more grip area.

problems.problem: The cups gape or fold at the top
problems.fix: The cup is too big or the wrong shape. Try one cup smaller or a molded cup that holds its own shape.
Try a style with a fabric-lined grip strip, or wear it for shorter periods. Stop wearing it if you develop a rash.

problems.problem: Wires dig in at the sides
problems.fix: Strapless wires sit further back. If they press on breast tissue, go up a cup; if they dig into ribs, look for a style with softer side boning.
Some firmness is expected, but heavy bulging means the band is too small or too narrow. Try a wider band or a longline.

extra.heading: Sister sizing and the firmer-band rule
extra.body: Because a strapless bra has to grip without help, the band should be the firmest of any bra you own. Sister sizes let you tighten the band without changing cup volume: 34B, 32C and 30D hold about the same volume, as do 36C, 34D and 32DD. If your regular 34C feels secure everywhere except strapless, try a 32D before buying a different style.

extra.heading: Making a strapless bra last
extra.body: Hand-wash and lay flat to dry so the silicone and boning keep their shape. Store it flat or folded at the band, never cup inside cup. Replace it when the grip strip loses tack, the band stretches, or it starts to slip in a size that used to stay put.

picks.label: Longline strapless bra
picks.why: The deeper band spreads the grip over more of your torso, which helps fuller busts stay secure for long events.

picks.label: Convertible multiway bra
picks.why: Wear it strapless with straps on standby, or switch to halter or crossover for different necklines.

picks.label: Adhesive backless bra
picks.why: For open-back or very low-cut outfits, mainly for smaller busts.

faqs.q: Should a strapless bra be tighter than a regular bra?
faqs.a: Yes. The band has no straps to help, so it should feel firmer. Many people go down one band size and up one cup letter for a strapless.

faqs.q: Should I size down in a strapless bra?
faqs.a: Size down the band, not the cup volume. Going from 34C to 32D keeps the cups the same while making the band tighter.

faqs.q: Why does my strapless bra keep falling down?
faqs.a: Almost always because the band is too loose. Gravity and the weight of the breasts pull it down unless the band grips firmly.

faqs.q: Can large busts wear strapless bras?
faqs.a: Yes. A longline, a wide-band underwire with tall side wings, or a convertible style with straps on standby usually works best.

faqs.q: How long can you wear a strapless bra?
faqs.a: A well-fitting one can be comfortable all day. If it pinches or slips after a few hours, the band size or style needs to change.
